newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Malaysia's Mahathir calls for calm in Cambodia.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia's Mahathir calls for calm in Cambodia.

text.p: Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad has written to Cambodian co-premiers Hun Sen and Prince Norodom Ranariddh stressing the need for political stability in Phnom Penh, officials said on Saturday.
The letter comes after weeks of tension between Hun Sen and Ranariddh, who formed an uneasy coalition after U.N.-sponsored elections in 1993.
"The letter expressed the need to ensure political stability in Cambodia," Hun Sen told Reuters on Saturday. An aide said the letter was delivered on Friday.
When asked if the letter was prompted by political tensions, Hun Sen said: "It is not advice. They are only interested in our taking care."
In addition to being the largest foreign investor in Cambodia, Malaysia is sponsoring Cambodia's bid to join the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN).
Cambodia, along with Laos and Burma, has observer status in the regional organisation, which groups Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam.
Cambodian officials hope to be granted membership by July 1997, but have expressed concern in recent weeks that tensions in the capital may delay the bid.
Political analysts said Mahathir's letter was prompted by the two premiers' disagreements over a broad range of issues, as well as Malaysia's stake in the country.
An adviser to Ranariddh said the co-premier had also received a letter from Mahathir, but only said it involved "international cooperation."

The co-premiers have been at odds over recruitment of Khmer Rouge guerrilla defectors, strains between troops loyal to each co-premier, and the fate of Prince Norodom Sirivudh, who has vowed to return after one year in exile for an alleged plot to assassinate Hun Sen.
In the past week, labour unrest flared in Phnom Penh, as 3,000 garment workers marched on the National Assembly to press for better working conditions.
